1	# REST API
     2	
     3	All endpoints are served by the built-in HTTP server on `serverPort` (default `4200`). Request and response bodies are JSON. The GUI SPA is served as static files from the same server.
     4	
     5	---
     6	
     7	## Repositories
     8	
     9	| Method | Path | Success | Error Codes | Description |
    10	|---|---|---|---|---|
    11	| `GET` | `/api/repositories` | 200 | — | List all repositories. |
    12	| `GET` | `/api/repositories/:id` | 200 | 404 | Get a single repository by ID. |
    13	| `POST` | `/api/repositories` | 201 | 400 | Register a new repository. Body: `{ url, name?, id? }`. |
    14	| `PUT` | `/api/repositories/:id` | 200 | 404, 500 | Update repository metadata. Body: `{ name }`. |
    15	| `DELETE` | `/api/repositories/:id` | 204 | 404 | Delete a repository. |
    16	| `PUT` | `/api/repositories/:id/credential` | 200 | 400, 404 | Assign or clear a git credential for a repository. Body: `{ credentialId: string \| null }`. |
    17	| `GET` | `/api/repositories/:id/credential-options` | 200 | 404 | List credentials compatible with the repository's host, with tokens masked. |
    18	
    19	### `PUT /api/repositories/:id/credential` — Assign or Clear a Credential
    20	
    21	Associates a configured git credential with a repository, or clears any existing association.
    22	
    23	**Request body:**
    24	
    25	| Field | Type | Required | Description |
    26	|---|---|---|---|
    27	| `credentialId` | `string \| null` | **Yes** | ID of the credential to assign. Pass `null` to clear the current association. Must reference an entry in `appConfig.gitCredentials` when a string. |
    28	
    29	**400 cases:**
    30	- `credentialId` is not a string and not `null` (e.g. missing field, number, boolean, object).
    31	- `credentialId` is a string that does not match any configured credential ID.
    32	- `credentialId` references a credential whose `host` does not match the repository URL's hostname (host-coherence guard). Example error: `Credential "my-cred" is configured for host "gitlab.com" but repository URL resolves to "github.com".`
    33	
    34	**404:** repository not found.
    35	
    36	**200 Response:** the full updated `Repository` object.
    37	
    38	> **Null-clear semantics:** when `credentialId` is `null`, the `CredentialId` field is **removed** from the persisted repository record entirely — it is not stored as `null`. A repository with no credential has no `CredentialId` key in its JSON.
    39	
    40	> **Host-coherence guard:** when assigning a credential, the API verifies that `credential.host` matches the hostname extracted from the repository URL. The check is skipped for SSH URLs (where `extractHost()` returns `null`) and when `credentialId` is `null` (clearing the association is always allowed). This prevents misrouted credential injection where a token for one host would be injected into git operations targeting a different host.
    41	
    42	> **Audit logging:** each successful assign or clear operation emits an audit log entry with `Source: 'credential-audit'` and `Operation: 'assign-credential'` or `'clear-credential'`. The `Context` field includes `{ RepositoryId: id }`. The credential token is never included in the audit entry.
    43	
    44	**Request body (assign):**
    45	```json
    46	{ "credentialId": "github-personal" }
    47	```
    48	
    49	**Request body (clear):**
    50	```json
    51	{ "credentialId": null }
    52	```
    53	
    54	**Response (200):**
    55	```json
    56	{
    57	    "Id": "my-repo",
    58	    "Url": "https://github.com/org/my-repo.git",
    59	    "Name": "my-repo",
    60	    "CredentialId": "github-personal"
    61	}
    62	```
    63	
    64	---
    65	
    66	### `GET /api/repositories/:id/credential-options` — List Compatible Credentials
    67	
    68	Returns the subset of configured git credentials whose `host` matches the repository's remote URL hostname. Tokens are always masked before being sent to the client.
    69	
    70	**404:** repository not found.
    71	
    72	**200 Response shape:**
    73	
    74	```json
    75	{
    76	    "credentials": [
    77	        { "id": "github-personal", "label": "GitHub personal account", "host": "github.com", "token": "***" }
    78	    ],
    79	    "autoSelected": "github-personal"
    80	}
    81	```
    82	
    83	| Field | Type | Description |
    84	|---|---|---|
    85	| `credentials` | `GitCredentialEntry[]` | Credentials whose `host` matches the repository URL's hostname. Tokens are replaced with `"***"`. Empty array `[]` when no credentials match or when the repository uses a non-HTTPS URL (e.g. SSH). |
    86	| `autoSelected` | `string` *(optional)* | ID of the sole matching credential. **Present only when `credentials` contains exactly one entry.** Omitted when zero or two-or-more credentials match. |
    87	
    88	> **SSH / non-HTTPS URLs:** repositories whose URL is not an HTTPS URL (e.g. `git@github.com:org/repo.git`) always return `{ "credentials": [] }` with no `autoSelected`. The host cannot be extracted from SSH URLs, so no credentials are ever shown for them.
    89	
    90	> **Known inconsistency — token mask format:** this endpoint masks tokens with the hardcoded string `"***"` (3 asterisks), while `GET /api/config/credentials` uses the `maskToken()` helper which produces `"****"` + last-4 characters (4 asterisks prefix, e.g. `"****abc1"`). Both surfaces guarantee the full token is never exposed; the format difference is a pre-existing inconsistency and will be unified in a future cleanup pass.
    91	
    92	---
    93	
    94	## Projects
    95	
    96	| Method | Path | Success | Error Codes | Description |
    97	|---|---|---|---|---|
    98	| `GET` | `/api/projects` | 200 | — | List all projects (index entries). |
    99	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:id` | 200 | 404 | Get full project data by ID. Response includes an optional `LastActivity?: string` field (ISO 8601) when the project has recorded git activity via the polling layer; absent on projects that have never been polled. |
   100	| `POST` | `/api/projects` | 201 | 400 | Create a new project. Body: `{ name, repositoryIds, description?, id? }`. |

1	/**
     2	 * Utility functions for resolving and injecting credentials into git remote URLs.
     3	 *
     4	 * Only HTTPS URLs are supported. SSH URLs (`git@...`) are left unchanged because
     5	 * SSH authentication is handled by the SSH agent or key — not by inline tokens.
     6	 *
     7	 * ## Credential resolution pipeline
     8	 *
     9	 * The intended call sequence for authenticated git operations is:
    10	 *
    11	 * 1. **{@link resolveCredential}** — given a repository URL and the configured
    12	 *    credential array, returns the matching {@link GitCredentialEntry} (or `null`
    13	 *    when resolution fails or is ambiguous).
    14	 * 2. **`entry.token`** — extract the token string from the resolved entry.
    15	 * 3. **{@link injectCredentialToken}** — embed the token into the URL as the
    16	 *    WHATWG URL username, producing an authenticated HTTPS URL ready for git.
    17	 *
    18	 * ```ts
    19	 * const entry = resolveCredential(repoUrl, config.gitCredentials, repo.CredentialId);
    20	 * const authenticatedUrl = entry ? injectCredentialToken(repoUrl, entry.token) : repoUrl;
    21	 * ```
    22	 *
    23	 */
    24	
    25	import type { GitCredentialEntry } from '../config/config.types.js';
    26	
    27	/**
    28	 * Extracts the hostname from an HTTPS git URL.
    29	 *
    30	 * @param url - The remote URL to inspect (e.g. "https://github.com/org/repo.git").
    31	 * @returns The hostname string (e.g. "github.com"), or `null` when the URL is
    32	 *   not a valid HTTPS URL (SSH, malformed, or empty).
    33	 */
    34	export function extractHost(url: string): string | null {
    35	    if (!url) return null;
    36	    try {
    37	        const parsed = new URL(url);
    38	        if (parsed.protocol !== 'https:') return null;
    39	        return parsed.hostname || null;
    40	    } catch {
    41	        return null;
    42	    }
    43	}
    44	
    45	/**
    46	 * Resolves the credential to use for a given repository URL.
    47	 *
    48	 * Resolution strategy:
    49	 *
    50	 * 1. **Explicit ID (`credentialId` provided):** Returns the entry whose `id`
    51	 *    matches `credentialId`, or `null` if no such entry exists (stale reference).
    52	 * 2. **Auto-selection (`credentialId` omitted):** Filters `credentials` by host
    53	 *    match against the URL's hostname.
    54	 *    - Exactly one match → returns that entry.
    55	 *    - Zero matches → returns `null` (no credentials configured for this host).
    56	 *    - Multiple matches → returns `null` (ambiguous; user must assign a
    57	 *      `CredentialId` to the repository explicitly).
    58	 *
    59	 * @param url          - The repository's remote URL.
    60	 * @param credentials  - The full array of configured credential entries.
    61	 * @param credentialId - Optional explicit credential ID to look up.
    62	 * @returns The matching `GitCredentialEntry`, or `null` when resolution fails.
    63	 *
    64	 * @remarks
    65	 * **SECURITY — host/credential coherence (explicit `credentialId` path):**
    66	 * When `credentialId` is supplied, resolution performs only an exact `id` match;
    67	 * no cross-validation against the URL's hostname is performed. A caller could
    68	 * inadvertently (or maliciously) pass a `credentialId` belonging to a different
    69	 * host and receive a credential for that host. The caller is responsible for
    70	 * ensuring the URL's host is consistent with the credential's configured `host`
    71	 * before using the resolved token. This validation should occur at the call site
    72	 * (e.g. in the orchestrators) before passing the authenticated URL to git.
    73	 */

    75	    url: string,
    76	    credentials: GitCredentialEntry[],

    78	): GitCredentialEntry | null {

1	# Constraints & Conventions
     2	
     3	## TypeScript Import Extensions
     4	
     5	All relative imports **must** include the `.js` extension:
     6	
     7	```typescript
     8	// Correct
     9	import { MyClass } from './my-module.js';
    10	
    11	// Wrong — compile error + runtime failure
    12	import { MyClass } from './my-module';
    13	```
    14	
    15	This is a strict requirement of the `Node16` module resolution setting. TypeScript maps `.js` → `.ts` at compile time and emits `.js` unchanged for Node.js at runtime.
    16	
    17	## Git Subprocess Security
    18	
    19	- All Git commands use `shell: false` — no shell expansion, globbing, or metacharacter processing.
    20	- Arguments are passed as a typed `string[]` directly to `spawn()`.
    21	- Error messages use only `args[0]` (the subcommand name), never the full args array, to avoid leaking credential-bearing URLs.
    22	- `RepositoryManager.add()` redacts embedded credentials from URLs before interpolating into error messages.
    23	- `runGit()` always sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `GIT_ASKPASS=echo` on every spawned subprocess. This prevents interactive credential prompts and credential-helper (osxkeychain, libsecret) blocking on unauthenticated requests. Do not remove either env var.
    24	- **Standing rule — credential stripping in git error output:** When credential injection is wired into future WPs (i.e., `injectCredentialToken()` is used to append tokens to URLs before passing to `runGit()`/`runGitOrThrow()`), all code paths that surface `GitResult.stderr` in thrown Error messages, log output, or API responses **must** apply `stripEmbeddedCredentials()` (from `src/git/git-credentials.ts`) to the stderr string first. Git may echo the credentialed URL back in error messages (e.g., `fatal: repository https://ghp_token@github.com/... not found`), which would expose the PAT. This is a non-optional security control for every credential-injection WP.
    25	- **Credential injection lifetime contract:** `injectCredentialToken()` must only be called immediately before a git subprocess invocation — never stored or returned through API boundaries. The injected URL must not appear in log output, API responses, or Error messages without first passing through `stripEmbeddedCredentials()`.
    26	- **Pre-embedded-credentials passthrough:** If a repo URL already contains embedded credentials (detected via `hasEmbeddedCredentials()`) orchestrator implementations **must** call `hasEmbeddedCredentials()` before invoking `resolveCredential()` + `injectCredentialToken()` and decide explicitly whether to strip and re-inject or reject the URL.- **Token masking rule (API responses):** The `gitCredentials` field in `AppConfig` / `config.json` stores **plaintext** tokens. No API handler, logger, or error message may expose a plaintext token in any response. All credential API responses must pass the array through `buildMaskedCredentials()` (in `src/server/routes/config.ts`) before serialisation — this applies `maskToken()` to every `token` field in each `GitCredentialEntry`, producing `****` + last-4-chars (e.g. `****abc1`). Tokens shorter than 4 characters are fully masked as `****`. This is a non-optional security control: any new credential endpoint **must** apply `buildMaskedCredentials()` before calling `sendJson()`.
    27	## Credential Field Validation
    28	
    29	### Hostname Format (`host` field)
    30	
    31	The `host` field in a `GitCredentialEntry` must not contain `/`, `\`, null bytes (`\0`), or whitespace characters. These characters are invalid in a hostname and are rejected with HTTP 400 by `PUT /api/config/credentials`. The validation regex is `/[/\\\0\s]/`. Valid examples: `github.com`, `gitlab.example.com`.
    32	
    33	### Per-Field Length Limits
    34	
    35	| Field | Maximum length |
    36	|---|---|
    37	| `id` | 100 characters |
    38	| `label` | 200 characters |
    39	| `host` | 253 characters |
    40	| `token` | 500 characters |
    41	
    42	These limits are enforced both at the API boundary (`PUT /api/config/credentials` → HTTP 400 on violation) and during config file parsing (`parseGitCredentials()` → `Error` thrown on violation). Values exactly at each limit are accepted.
    43	
    44	**API whitespace normalization:** `PUT /api/config/credentials` trims leading and trailing whitespace from `id`, `label`, and `token` before storage. This is intentional UX normalization (e.g., clipboard pastes with trailing newlines). The stored value may therefore differ from what was submitted. The `host` field is handled differently: whitespace is rejected outright (HTTP 400) rather than stripped, because whitespace is structurally invalid in a hostname.
    45	
    46	**Config parser non-normalization:** `parseGitCredentials()` applies `.trim()` only to *measure* field length during validation — it does not normalize the values it returns. The in-memory `GitCredentialEntry[]` array reflects the raw strings from `config.json`, including any surrounding whitespace. Code that consumes parsed credentials should trim field values before use if the config.json source is untrusted or manually edited. The API route handler, by contrast, always produces and stores clean (trimmed) values.
    47	
    48	### Host/Credential Coherence (`PUT /api/repositories/:id/credential`)
    49	
    50	When assigning a credential to a repository, the API validates that `credential.host` matches the hostname extracted from the repository's URL via `extractHost()`. If they do not match, the request is rejected with HTTP 400 and a descriptive error message indicating both the credential's host and the repository URL's host. This guard prevents silent credential misrouting. The check is skipped when:
    51	- `credentialId` is `null` (clearing the association is always allowed).
    52	- The repository URL is not an HTTPS URL (SSH URLs return `null` from `extractHost()`).
    53	
    54	## Stateless Managers
    55	
    56	All model managers (`RepositoryManager`, `ProjectManager`, `WorkspaceManager`) re-read their backing JSON file from disk on **every** public method call. There is no in-memory cache. This ensures concurrent writes from other processes are always reflected.
    57	
    58	## ID Validation Rules
    59	
    60	| Entity | Format | Validation Function |
    61	|---|---|---|
    62	| Repository ID | Lowercase kebab-case (`a-z0-9`, segments separated by `-`) | `isValidKebabCase()` |
    63	| Project ID | Lowercase kebab-case | `isValidKebabCase()` |
    64	| Workspace ID | 2–10 uppercase ASCII letters (`A-Z`) | `isValidWorkspaceId()` |
    65	
    66	Path-traversal sequences, uppercase characters (for kebab-case IDs), spaces, and other invalid formats are rejected with a descriptive error.
    67	
    68	## The STABLE Workspace Invariant
    69	
    70	Every project has exactly one workspace with ID `"STABLE"`. It is auto-created when a project is created and **cannot be removed or renamed**. The STABLE workspace is intended for the remote's default branch.
    71	
    72	## Path Resolution
    73	
    74	Both `storageFolder` and `projectsFolder` in `config.json` accept relative or absolute paths:
    75	
    76	- **Relative paths** are resolved against the tool root (directory containing `package.json`), regardless of the current working directory when the tool is invoked.
    77	- **Absolute paths** are used as-is.
    78	
    79	## Configuration
    80	
    81	- `config.json` is created by copying `config.dist.json`. It is not committed (gitignored).
    82	- The `_instructions` key in `config.dist.json` is an editorial note and is not a valid config field. Remove it from `config.json`.
    83	- `initializeStorage()` is idempotent — re-running it does not overwrite existing files.
    84	- **`DEFAULTS` Pick maintenance:** The exported `DEFAULTS` constant in `src/config/config.ts` is typed as `Pick<AppConfig, 'cloneDepth' | 'serverPort' | 'gitPollingIntervalSeconds' | 'notesCardHeight' | 'notesColumns'>`. When a new non-optional, non-required `AppConfig` field with a sensible default is added, **three** coordinated changes are required: (1) add the field key to the `Pick` union, (2) add the field's default value to the `DEFAULTS` object literal, and (3) add the fallback guard in `loadConfig()` (e.g. `typeof raw['field'] === 'number' ? raw['field'] : DEFAULTS.field`). Omitting step (1) is a TypeScript compile error; omitting steps (2)–(3) causes the field to be `undefined` at runtime for configs that predate the new field.
    85	- **`_defaultsCoverageGuard` pattern:** Immediately after `DEFAULTS`, a `const _defaultsCoverageGuard: AppConfig = { ...DEFAULTS, projectsFolder: '', storageFolder: '' } satisfies AppConfig` expression is declared and voided. The `satisfies AppConfig` clause is a compile-time completeness guard: if a new required field is added to `AppConfig` without a corresponding entry in `DEFAULTS` or the guard literal, TypeScript emits a type error at that exact line. Do not remove this guard — it is the automated enforcement mechanism for the DEFAULTS maintenance rule above.
    86	
    87	## Schema Version Policy
    88	
    89	The `SchemaVersion` field on `BaseStore` tracks structural changes to persisted JSON store files. The rule is defined in `src/storage/storage.types.ts`:
    90	
    91	- **Do NOT bump `SCHEMA_VERSION`** when adding an **optional** field. Existing JSON files that lack the field are still valid — no migration is required.
    92	- **Do bump `SCHEMA_VERSION`** (and add a migration step) for breaking changes: removing a required field, renaming a field, or changing the type of an existing field in a way that would cause older JSON files to fail validation or produce incorrect behaviour.
    93	
    94	**Example:** `Repository.CredentialId` is an optional field addition — existing `repositories.json` files remain valid without it. No `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump was needed for this change.
    95	
    96	## Test Conventions
    97	
    98	- **Test runner:** Node.js built-in test runner (`node --test`).
    99	- **Cleanup:** All tests creating temporary files must register a `process.on('exit')` handler for synchronous cleanup, in addition to `afterAll`. The `'exit'` event fires on `SIGINT` or crash.
   100	- **Network tests:** Tests requiring outbound internet set `SKIP_NETWORK_TESTS=1` to self-skip.
